title: Infrastructure as Code: Terraform and Bicep
oneLiner: Describe cloud infrastructure in reviewed, versioned code, and learn to read a Terraform plan before it deletes your database.
keyTakeaway: IaC tools compare the code with what exists and change the difference. Terraform tracks what it manages in a state file that should live in a shared, locked backend; Bicep uses Azure's own records. Always read the plan: + creates, ~ updates in place, -/+ replaces (and a replaced database is empty), - destroys.
explanation:
Clicking resources together in a portal can't be reviewed, repeated or rebuilt. This lesson shows the same Azure web app in Terraform and in Bicep, explains state, plan and apply, and compares the tools.

The plan simulator replays real Terraform 1.9.8 runs: a first apply, an in-place update, a forced replacement, drift, and a rename with and without a moved block. The Azure Terraform passes terraform validate and the Bicep file compiles with bicep build.
